title: Proactive IT Management with a Predictive Maintenance System
content: This research addresses the challenge of predictive maintenance in IT systems by developing and evaluating models that accurately identify and classify failure types, crucial for preemptive action in maintenance. To achieve this, we designed a hybrid CNN-LSTM model to capture complex temporal and spatial patterns in system data, essential for detecting nuanced failure dynamics. This model was benchmarked against traditional models, including Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forests, and Support Vector Machines (SVM). We used the SMOTE technique to address class imbalances, which improved the training process and enabled the model to detect minority failure types more effectively. Our CNN-LSTM hybrid model achieved a notable accuracy of 92.4%, outperforming conventional models by better leveraging multi-dimensional data attributes. Confusion matrices showed high precision across most failure classes, though the model’s lowest precision was 86% for random failures. ROC and Precision-Recall curves with areas consistently above 0.90 further validated the model’s robustness. Although effective, the class imbalance issue still impacted precision and recall for infrequent failure types. Significant predictors, including rotational speed and process temperature, were identified, highlighting their role in failure detection. We improve IT systems’ predictive maintenance with such hybrid approach, which is a good candidate for handling complex failure modes. In conclusion, this paper has proposed a CNN-LSTM hybrid model that will enhance IT predictive maintenance by detecting and classifying failure types accurately leading to the application of aiding IT managers with optimum maintenance strategies.
